strengths: Clearly identifies and addresses two concrete limitations of the SOTA F3Loc method: lack of uncertainty modeling and reliance on per-environment depth network training.

Extensive empirical evaluation across three datasets (synthetic Gibson, synthetic Structured3D, real-world LaMAR HGE/CAB) for both sequential and single-frame localization, with substantial reported improvements especially in the challenging real-world LaMAR setting (up to 16.7x recall improvement on short sequences).

Thorough ablation studies: uncertainty vs. no uncertainty, different pretrained monodepth encoders (DINOv2, DepthPro, Depth Anything V2 at multiple scales), grid resolution trade-offs, and observation-update frequency for runtime reduction.
Cross-domain generalization experiment (train on HGE, test on CAB) demonstrating that the pretrained-depth approach transfers better than F3Loc's custom-trained depth network.

Principled probabilistic formulation (Laplace observation model, NLL loss) that cleanly integrates uncertainty into the existing histogram-filter framework, with a clear description of how uncertainty propagates through the Bayesian update.
Efficiency analysis (accuracy vs. model size/runtime) showing favorable trade-offs even with smaller pretrained encoders.
Good qualitative visualizations (observation likelihoods, posterior evolution) that support the quantitative claims.
weaknesses: Methodological novelty is fairly incremental: the core architecture (masked attention, histogram filter) is directly inherited from F3Loc, and the two additions -- standard heteroscedastic Laplace uncertainty and swapping in an off-the-shelf pretrained depth encoder -- are individually well-established techniques rather than fundamentally new ideas.

On several single-frame localization metrics (Gibson(t), Structured3D), the uncertainty-aware variant is actually slightly worse than the non-uncertainty variant, and the explanation given (uncertainty only helps in sequential fusion) is plausible but not rigorously verified with additional analysis.

Test set sizes for LaMAR HGE at longer sequence lengths are quite small (e.g., N=11 for T=100, N=37 for Gibson), which limits the statistical robustness of the headline multiplicative improvement claims (2.7x, 16.7x).

In the cross-domain LaMAR CAB experiment, while success-rate (SR) numbers look strong, the underlying recall numbers in the supplementary (e.g., ~2.5% recall at 1m) reveal the absolute localization accuracy is still quite poor, suggesting the generalization claim is more nuanced than the main text implies.

The method incurs substantially higher per-frame runtime (up to ~1s on LaMAR) due to using a heavier pretrained depth network and matching step; while partially mitigated via grid coarsening and reduced observation frequency, this remains a practical drawback relative to F3Loc's lightweight custom network, and is somewhat downplayed in the main narrative.
Limited discussion of failure cases or sensitivity to gravity/intrinsics estimation errors (e.g., when GeoCalib is used instead of sensor data), despite this being a stated real-world use case.
Missing direct comparison to some other floorplan localization baselines (e.g., LaLaLoc++) on the same benchmarks; only LASER and PF-Net numbers are borrowed from prior work for a subset of datasets.

strengths: Well-motivated approach addressing two clear limitations of the prior SOTA (F3Loc): lack of uncertainty modeling and per-dataset depth network training. The proposed solutions (Laplace-distributed uncertainty-aware depth prediction and off-the-shelf monodepth features) are simple, principled, and clearly explained.

Strong and comprehensive empirical results: large improvements over F3Loc on both synthetic (Gibson) and challenging real-world (LaMAR HGE, including the full uncropped scene) datasets, with especially dramatic gains on short sequences (42.2x SR improvement on 15-frame sequences), which is practically important for fast localization.

Extensive ablations: encoder choice (DINOv2, DepthPro, Depth Anything v2 at multiple sizes) with and without uncertainty, Laplace vs Gaussian uncertainty modeling, grid resolution vs runtime trade-offs, observation update frequency, single-frame vs sequential localization, and cross-domain generalization (HGE->CAB) with/without fine-tuning — providing thorough evidence for each design choice.

Good engineering/practical considerations: gravity alignment for handheld devices, lightweight uncertainty-weighted post-processing optimization, and runtime analysis showing the method remains near real-time.
Reasonably strong reproducibility statement with code, dataset preprocessing details, and training details provided in appendix.
The paper is honest about limitations, e.g., higher computational cost of off-the-shelf depth encoder, and provides mitigations (frame-skipping, coarser grid) with quantified trade-offs.
weaknesses: Novelty is somewhat incremental: the core architecture (masked attention, histogram filter, ray-based matching) is directly borrowed from F3Loc, with the main contributions being (a) swapping in a pretrained monodepth encoder and (b) adding an aleatoric uncertainty head with a standard Laplace/Gaussian NLL formulation, both of which are well-established techniques in other depth/localization contexts (e.g., Kendall & Gal 2017, Roessle et al. 2022).

The custom-constructed LaMAR HGE/CAB 2D floorplan ground truth relies on a manually calibrated affine transformation (4 doorway point pairs) with no independent ground-truth verification beyond qualitative consistency checks (residuals, raycast depth matching), which introduces some uncertainty into the reported real-world numbers.

Comparison to F3Loc on LaMAR uses a self-trained F3Loc model (since no official checkpoint exists for this dataset), which is reasonable but leaves open the possibility that F3Loc's poor performance partly reflects suboptimal retraining/hyperparameters rather than a fundamental limitation, especially given the very large performance gap (e.g., 0% success in Table 4).

Only one real-world building (LaMAR HGE/CAB, same underlying campus/dataset family) is used for real-world evaluation; broader real-world diversity (different buildings, sensor types, more heterogeneous conditions) would strengthen generalization claims.

Epistemic uncertainty is explicitly not modeled (acknowledged by the authors), which could matter more for true out-of-distribution/zero-shot floorplan generalization claims than the cross-domain LaMAR HGE->CAB experiment (which the authors themselves note is not a strict zero-shot setting since the same sensor/dataset family is used).

Runtime is meaningfully higher than F3Loc on LaMAR (~1s/frame due to depth encoder and matching), which is only partially mitigated by proposed tricks (frame skipping, coarser grid) and could limit real-time deployment on resource-constrained AR/mobile devices, a key motivating use case.
